claims: Artemis II is a ~10-day crewed mission scheduled for April 2026.
Artemis II uses a "hybrid free-return trajectory".
Artemis II loops around the Moon and returns to Earth without landing.
Artemis II launches from Kennedy Space Center on the SLS rocket.
The Orion spacecraft performs Earth-orbit checkouts.
The Orion spacecraft performs a trans-lunar injection.
The Orion spacecraft performs a far-side flyby.
The Orion spacecraft splashes down in the Pacific Ocean.
The SLS launches from Kennedy Space Center on Day 1 of Artemis II.
The SLS places Orion into a high elliptical orbit.
The crew performs a ~23-hour checkout on Day 1 of Artemis II.
The checkout conducts proximity operations to test manual handling.
On Day 2 of Artemis II, Orion’s service module performs a burn to boost the spacecraft from Earth orbit toward the Moon.
The spacecraft travels to the Moon during Days 3-6 of Artemis II.
The spacecraft enters the lunar sphere of influence on day 5 of Artemis II.
The spacecraft performs a flyby on day 6 of Artemis II.
The flyby flies approximately 3,000 to 9,000 miles above the far side of the Moon.
The Artemis II flyby sets records for human distance from Earth.
Artemis II uses a "free-return" trajectory.
The Moon's gravity swings the capsule back toward Earth in Artemis II.
Artemis II splashes down in the Pacific Ocean on day 10.
Artemis II crew members are Wiseman, Glover, Koch, and Hansen.
The crew is aboard the Integrity capsule.
Artemis II acts as the final crewed test for the Artemis program.
